notes: Author page 14; archive folio 92. The page continues an action-on-a-system discussion, states uniqueness of a lifted action and an extra object-set stability condition, then considers lifts without a prescribed fixed primed point. Formula (46) expresses compatibility with the group action. The page ends with the live continuation En termes.

The small oblique note assumes an unprimed fixed x₀. The longer note says the first construction does not require connectedness, whereas the later subgroup description depends on it. This is a synopsis of the manuscript, not a checked theorem.

Every C/H token, including agreements, was compared against the ink in the two native halves. Abbreviations, the incomplete cancelled prolong, distinct H-index parentheses, primes, zero indices, star, dots, underlines, cancellations and insertion attachments were retained literally.

The final addition contains two levels: an upper cancelled puisque plus a tentative expression, and a lower live x'∈E₀ preceded by an uncertain short form. Pr is tentative. The apparent forall may be formed by crossing descenders rather than an independent quantifier; it is not certified.
The isolated near-vertical stroke beside the long note is a margin divider with no label or arrow, reproduced in TikZ rather than treated as a mathematical diagram.
The first reader performed visual transcription rather than a mathematical proof check. A separately recorded main-reader check of the uniqueness assertion follows.

Whole page viewed once and native halves once each. Eleven distinct open loci received one crop each. The small note was rotated -39 degrees and the long note -42 degrees; all other crops have rotation 0. Original crop boxes are given without pretending that rotated-image coordinates are original coordinates.

Root check 142-093-R1 verifies the author’s uniqueness claim after (46): on a transitive G-set, semilinearity forces F(gx0)=alpha(g)F(x0), so one value determines F. This does not assert that every value defines a map, and does not settle the crowded final insertion by mathematical expectation.

The main reader checked all substantive disagreements on the saved crops, including twelve additional first crops of loci settled by the first reader on the halves. The existing long-margin crop was reused to confirm four dark points after connexité. No second crop of a decided place was made.

The full second reading marks the second inserted Θ with bar/flattened-tilde uncertainty, independently of the first insertion’s tilde/prime ambiguity. The near-flat detached stroke is visually distinct from the nearby wave over C; no new mathematical object is inferred.

The abbreviation before satisfaisant reads i.e with its internal point and no visible terminal point. The separate f. and s. points remain. No independent terminal point is found after the last connexe in the oblique margin, so none is supplied.

Two tiny dark points stand high to the right of the left closing parenthesis of (46), above the ordinary equality. Their visible arrangement is reproduced in a small inline TikZ drawing. Their function remains unresolved between punctuation-like traces and incidental pen-points; neither a colon nor defining equality is asserted. The drawing has a separate inventory entry, not an invented word.

The closing connai-t has a compact hooked i mark and retains plain i first with a circumflex alternative. Nine inherited text doubts and these two new text doubts remain. No new mathematical check event.

check_events.outcome: The uniqueness assertion after (46) was checked under the displayed homogeneity hypothesis. If a group G acts transitively on E and F satisfies F(gx)=alpha(g)F(x), choose x0 in E. Every x=gx0, so F(x)=alpha(g)F(x0). Thus at most one such F has a prescribed value at x0. The assertion is uniqueness only; an arbitrary proposed value need not satisfy the stabilizer condition needed for existence. No handwritten symbol was repaired from this argument.
